Computable answers (binary subtraction, octal, one's complement, Gray code, pipeline cycles, DDR4 bandwidth, Round Robin, LRU, umask, audio size, print size, TB vs GiB, disk capacity, subnet sizing, IPv6 compression, Caesar cipher, SQL NOT BETWEEN with NULL via sqlite3, Excel LARGE, INDEX/MATCH, COUNTIFS, SUMPRODUCT) are re-derived in tools/batch_003/computer.py. Shortcuts and protocol facts were checked on Microsoft Support, RFC Editor and MDN pages on 2026-11-05; exFAT, Freeze Panes, #REF!, PCI DSS and UEFI were confirmed from search results only (web:search-confirmed).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: ENIAC, completed in 1945 and one of the earliest general-purpose electronic digital computers, used about 18,000 vacuum tubes. To which generation of computers does it belong?

solution.explanation: Computers built with vacuum tubes form the first generation (roughly 1940s to mid-1950s). ENIAC is the best-known example, along with UNIVAC I.
steps: ENIAC used vacuum tubes, so it is a first-generation computer
solution.why_others_wrong: Second-generation machines used transistors, third-generation used integrated circuits and fourth-generation use microprocessors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What is the result of the binary subtraction 110010 - 10111?

solution.explanation: 110010 is 50 and 10111 is 23 in decimal. 50 - 23 = 27, and 27 = 16 + 8 + 2 + 1 = 11011 in binary. Done directly in binary, each borrow from the next column brings in 2 (binary 10).
solution.shortcut: Convert both to decimal, subtract, convert back.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10011 = 19, 11001 = 25 and 11111 = 31; each comes from a missed or extra borrow.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What is the octal (base 8) equivalent of the decimal number 100?

solution.concept: Decimal to octal by repeated division by 8
solution.explanation: Divide by 8 and read the remainders from the last to the first: 100 / 8 = 12 r 4, 12 / 8 = 1 r 4, 1 / 8 = 0 r 1. Reading upwards gives 144. Check: 1 x 64 + 4 x 8 + 4 = 100.
solution.why_others_wrong: 64 is 100 written in hexadecimal, not octal (read as octal, 64 is only 52). 124 (octal) = 84 and 154 (octal) = 108.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What is the one's complement of the 8-bit binary number 10110100?

solution.explanation: The one's complement is formed by inverting every bit: each 1 becomes 0 and each 0 becomes 1. 10110100 becomes 01001011.
solution.shortcut: One's complement = flip every bit; two's complement = one's complement + 1.
solution.why_others_wrong: 01001100 is the two's complement (one's complement + 1). 00101101 is the original bits reversed in order, not inverted. 10110101 only adds 1 to the original number.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A hospital ICU machine measures a patient's heartbeat and blood pressure as continuous signals and then converts them into digital readings that are processed and displayed as numbers. Which type of computer combines both these features?

solution.explanation: A hybrid computer combines the analog ability to measure continuously varying quantities with the digital ability to process and display them as exact numbers. ICU monitoring equipment and petrol pump dispensers are standard examples.
steps: Numerical processing and display = digital feature
solution.why_others_wrong: An analog computer alone does not produce digital processing, and a purely digital computer cannot take the continuous signal directly. 'Mainframe' describes size and number of users, not the kind of data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In which generation of computers did transistors replace vacuum tubes and high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL come into wide use?

solution.explanation: The second generation (roughly 1956 to 1963) used transistors, which were smaller, faster, cooler and more reliable than vacuum tubes. High-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL became common in this period, replacing much machine-language programming.
steps: FORTRAN and COBOL spread in the same period
solution.why_others_wrong: The first generation used vacuum tubes and machine language. The third generation is known for integrated circuits and the fifth for artificial intelligence.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In Gray code, consecutive values differ in exactly one bit. A binary number is converted to Gray code by keeping the most significant bit and then XOR-ing each pair of adjacent bits. What is the Gray code of the decimal number 13?

solution.explanation: 13 = 1101 in binary. Keep the first bit (1). Then XOR adjacent bits: 1 XOR 1 = 0, 1 XOR 0 = 1, 0 XOR 1 = 1. The Gray code is 1011. Equivalently, Gray = n XOR (n >> 1) = 1101 XOR 0110 = 1011.
solution.shortcut: Gray = binary XOR (binary shifted right by one place).
solution.why_others_wrong: 1101 is plain binary for 13, not Gray code. 1110 is the Gray code of 11. 1001 comes from XOR-ing the wrong pairs of bits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which unit inside a desktop cabinet converts the AC mains supply from the wall socket into the low-voltage DC needed by the motherboard and drives?

solution.explanation: The SMPS (Switched-Mode Power Supply) is the computer's internal power supply unit. It converts AC mains into regulated DC voltages such as 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V for the components.
steps: AC from wall -> DC for components = SMPS
solution.why_others_wrong: A UPS provides backup power during outages and sits outside the cabinet. The CMOS battery only keeps the clock and firmware settings. A voltage stabiliser evens out mains voltage but does not convert AC to DC.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of the heat sink and fan fixed on top of a computer's processor?

options.text: To carry heat away from the CPU so it does not overheat
To increase the CPU's clock speed
To store frequently used data close to the CPU
To supply electrical power to the CPU

solution.explanation: A processor produces heat while it works. The metal heat sink absorbs this heat and the fan blows it away. Without cooling, the CPU slows itself down (throttles) or shuts down to avoid damage.
steps: Heat sink + fan = cooling the CPU
solution.why_others_wrong: Cooling does not raise the clock speed by itself, caching is the job of cache memory, and power comes from the power supply through the motherboard.
solution.final_answer: Option A: To carry heat away from the CPU so it does not overheat

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which 15-pin, D-shaped port carries only analog video signals and is found on older monitors and projectors?

solution.explanation: VGA (Video Graphics Array) uses a 15-pin D-sub connector and carries analog video only, with no audio. It is being replaced by digital ports such as HDMI and DisplayPort.
solution.why_others_wrong: HDMI and USB Type-C carry digital signals. RJ-45 is the Ethernet network connector.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A processor is described as '64-bit'. This figure refers to its:

options.text: Word size: the number of bits it processes as one unit
Amount of cache memory in kilobytes

solution.concept: Word size (word length) of a CPU
solution.explanation: Word size is the number of bits a CPU handles as one unit in its registers and ALU operations. A 64-bit processor works on 64-bit chunks of data and can use 64-bit memory addresses.
steps: 'n-bit processor' = word size of n bits
solution.why_others_wrong: Clock speed is measured in GHz, cores are counted separately (dual-core, quad-core) and cache is measured in KB or MB.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Word size: the number of bits it processes as one unit

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A processor has a 5-stage instruction pipeline, and each stage takes one clock cycle. Ignoring stalls and hazards, how many clock cycles are needed to complete 100 instructions?

solution.explanation: In a k-stage pipeline the first instruction needs k cycles to pass through every stage. After that, one instruction finishes every cycle. So n instructions need k + (n - 1) cycles: 5 + 99 = 104.
steps: Each of the remaining 99 instructions: 1 more cycle
solution.shortcut: Pipeline cycles = k + n - 1; without a pipeline = k x n.
solution.why_others_wrong: 100 ignores the cycles needed to fill the pipeline. 105 adds one cycle too many. 500 is the time without pipelining (5 x 100).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a typical feature of a RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) processor, compared with a CISC processor?

options.text: Simple fixed-length instructions, most completing in one cycle, with only load and store instructions accessing memory
Many complex variable-length instructions that can operate directly on memory
Fewer general-purpose registers so that instructions can be longer
Heavy use of microcode to run each complex instruction in many cycles

solution.explanation: RISC designs use a small set of simple, fixed-length instructions that pipeline well, usually finish in one cycle, and follow a load/store design: only load and store touch memory, all other operations work on registers. ARM processors in phones are RISC; x86 processors are CISC.
solution.why_others_wrong: Complex variable-length instructions that work directly on memory, and multi-cycle microcoded instructions, describe CISC. RISC processors usually have more registers, not fewer.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Simple fixed-length instructions, most completing in one cycle, with only load and store instructions accessing memory

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A DDR4-3200 memory module performs 3,200 million transfers per second on a 64-bit wide memory bus. What is its peak data transfer rate (1 GB = 10^9 bytes)?

solution.concept: Memory bandwidth = transfer rate x bus width
solution.explanation: Each transfer moves 64 bits = 8 bytes. 3,200 x 10^6 transfers per second x 8 bytes = 25,600 x 10^6 bytes per second = 25.6 GB/s. This is why DDR4-3200 modules are also labelled PC4-25600.
solution.shortcut: MT/s x 8 = MB/s for a 64-bit module (3200 x 8 = 25600).
solution.why_others_wrong: 3.2 GB/s forgets that each transfer carries 8 bytes. 12.8 GB/s halves the rate (the 'double' in DDR is already inside the 3,200 MT/s figure). 51.2 GB/s doubles it again or assumes two channels.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Antivirus programs, disk clean-up tools and file-compression tools such as a ZIP utility are classified as:

solution.explanation: Utility software is system software that helps maintain, protect and optimise the computer. Antivirus, backup, disk clean-up and compression tools are utilities.
steps: Maintaining and protecting the system = utility software
solution.why_others_wrong: Application software does user tasks such as writing letters or making spreadsheets. Programming languages are used to write programs. Firmware is software stored permanently in a device's chip.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The permanent software stored in a flash or ROM chip of a device such as a router or printer, which controls the device's basic functions, is called:

solution.explanation: Firmware is software built into a hardware device's non-volatile chip. It controls the device at a low level and is changed only by a firmware update. BIOS/UEFI is the firmware of a PC.
steps: Software stored permanently in a device's chip = firmware
solution.why_others_wrong: Freeware and shareware are licensing models. Middleware is software that connects applications to each other or to databases.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Software whose author has given up all copyright, so that anyone may use, copy and change it without any restriction, is called:

solution.explanation: Public domain software has no copyright owner, so there are no licence conditions at all. Open-source software, by contrast, is still copyrighted but released under a licence.
steps: No copyright, no restrictions = public domain
solution.why_others_wrong: Proprietary software is owned and restricted by its publisher. Shareware and trial software are copyrighted and must be paid for after a trial.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An interest-calculation program compiles and runs without any error message, but it prints wrong interest amounts because the formula multiplies by the rate instead of dividing it by 100. What kind of error is this?

solution.explanation: A logic error lets the program run but makes it produce wrong results because the instructions themselves are wrong. The compiler cannot detect it; it is found by testing.
steps: Program runs + output wrong = logic error
solution.why_others_wrong: Syntax and compilation errors stop the program from compiling. A linker error occurs when a referenced function or library cannot be found while building the executable.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: While installing a proprietary application, the user must click 'I Agree' to a legal contract stating how the software may be used. This contract is called the:

solution.explanation: The EULA is the agreement between the software publisher and the user. It sets out how many devices the software may be installed on, and what the user may not do, such as copying or reverse-engineering it.
solution.why_others_wrong: The GPL is an open-source licence. An SLA sets service levels (such as uptime) between a provider and a client. An NDA is a confidentiality agreement.
solution.final_answer: Option D: EULA (End User License Agreement)

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Assembly language, which uses mnemonics such as ADD and MOV, belongs to which generation of programming languages?

solution.explanation: 1GL is machine language (binary). 2GL is assembly language with mnemonics. 3GL covers high-level languages such as C, Java and Python. 4GL covers languages closer to human requests, such as SQL.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1GL is pure binary machine code. 3GL and 4GL are high-level languages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's data centre runs several operating systems at the same time on one physical server, each in its own virtual machine. Which software layer makes this possible?

solution.explanation: A hypervisor (virtual machine monitor) divides one physical machine's CPU, memory and storage among several virtual machines, each running its own operating system.
steps: Several OSes on one physical server = virtual machines
solution.why_others_wrong: A compiler translates programs, a device driver lets the OS control one piece of hardware, and a browser displays web pages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In an object-oriented program, the balance of an Account object is declared private and can be changed only through the object's deposit() and withdraw() methods. Which OOP principle does this show?

solution.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data with the methods that act on it and hides the data from outside code. Other code cannot set the balance directly; it must go through the controlled methods.
steps: Private data + access only through methods = encapsulation
solution.why_others_wrong: Inheritance lets a class reuse another class's members. Polymorphism lets one method name behave differently for different classes. Compilation is translation, not an OOP principle.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which phase of a compiler reads the source program character by character and groups the characters into tokens such as keywords, identifiers, operators and constants?

solution.explanation: Lexical analysis (scanning) is the first phase. It removes spaces and comments and turns the character stream into tokens. The parser then checks whether the tokens form valid grammar, and later phases optimise and generate machine code.
steps: Then semantic analysis, optimisation, code generation
solution.why_others_wrong: Syntax analysis works on tokens, not characters. Optimisation and code generation come near the end of compilation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In Windows, which keyboard shortcut opens File Explorer?

solution.explanation: Windows logo key + E opens File Explorer. Windows logo key + D shows or hides the desktop and Windows logo key + I opens Settings.
solution.why_others_wrong: Win + D shows the desktop, Win + I opens Settings and Win + R opens the Run dialog.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Windows logo key + E

fact_checks.claim: Windows logo key + E opens File Explorer; + D displays and hides the desktop; + I opens Settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which Linux command displays the full path of the directory you are currently working in?

solution.explanation: pwd (print working directory) prints the full path of the current directory, for example /home/asha/reports.
solution.why_others_wrong: cd changes the directory, ls lists its contents and mkdir creates a new directory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An operating system interface in which the user types commands at a prompt, such as the Windows Command Prompt or a Linux terminal, is called a:

solution.concept: User interfaces of an operating system
solution.explanation: In a command-line interface the user types text commands and the system replies in text. In a GUI the user works with windows, icons and menus using a mouse or touch.
steps: Typed commands at a prompt = CLI
solution.why_others_wrong: A GUI uses icons and windows, a touch interface uses taps and gestures, and a menu-driven interface lets the user pick from listed choices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A computer with too little RAM spends most of its time moving pages between main memory and the disk, so programs become extremely slow even though the CPU is busy with paging. This condition is called:

solution.explanation: Thrashing happens when processes do not have enough frames for the pages they are actively using. Page faults become so frequent that the system does more swapping than useful work.
steps: Constant paging + very little useful work = thrashing
solution.why_others_wrong: Deadlock is processes waiting for each other's resources. Spooling queues jobs (for example print jobs) on disk. Fragmentation is wasted or scattered storage space.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Microsoft designed which file system as the successor to FAT32, intended for flash media such as USB drives and SD cards, and able to store individual files larger than 4 GB?

solution.concept: File systems for removable flash media
solution.explanation: exFAT (Extended File Allocation Table) succeeds FAT32 in the FAT family. It uses 64 bits to describe file size, so it removes FAT32's 4 GB per-file limit while staying simple enough for cameras, SD cards and pen drives.
steps: Successor to FAT32 + flash media + files over 4 GB = exFAT
solution.why_others_wrong: FAT16 is older and more limited than FAT32. ext4 is a Linux file system and HFS+ an older Apple file system; neither was designed by Microsoft.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft's exFAT specification describes exFAT as the successor to FAT32 in the FAT family; exFAT uses 64 bits to describe file size, lifting FAT32's 4 GB file-size limit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Processes P1, P2 and P3 arrive at time 0 in that order with CPU burst times of 10 ms, 4 ms and 6 ms. They are scheduled by Round Robin with a time quantum of 4 ms. What is the average waiting time?

solution.explanation: Gantt chart: P1 0-4, P2 4-8 (done), P3 8-12, P1 12-16, P3 16-18 (done), P1 18-20 (done). Waiting time = completion time - burst time: P1 = 20 - 10 = 10, P2 = 8 - 4 = 4, P3 = 18 - 6 = 12. Average = 26 / 3 = 8.67 ms.
solution.shortcut: With all arrivals at 0, waiting time = completion time - burst time.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.67 ms is the Shortest Job First result, 8.00 ms is FCFS, and 15.33 ms is the average turnaround time, not the waiting time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A system has 3 page frames, all empty at the start. Using LRU (Least Recently Used) page replacement, how many page faults occur for the reference string 2, 5, 2, 8, 6, 5, 2, 8, 6?

solution.explanation: LRU removes the page that has not been used for the longest time. 2 F, 5 F, 2 hit, 8 F (frames 2, 5, 8). 6 F replaces 5 (least recent) -> 2, 8, 6. 5 F replaces 2 -> 8, 6, 5. 2 F replaces 8 -> 6, 5, 2. 8 F replaces 6 -> 5, 2, 8. 6 F replaces 5 -> 2, 8, 6. Total 8 faults.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 is what FIFO and the Optimal algorithm both give for this string, not LRU. 7 comes from evicting a wrong page at one step. 9 counts the hit on the third reference (page 2) as a fault.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the four necessary (Coffman) conditions for a deadlock?

options.text: Preemption: the OS can take a resource away from a process holding it

solution.explanation: A deadlock can occur only if all four hold: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, NO preemption and circular wait. If resources can be preempted, the cycle can be broken, so preemption prevents deadlock rather than causing it.
steps: Four conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait
Preemption is the opposite of 'no preemption'
solution.why_others_wrong: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait and circular wait are all necessary conditions.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Preemption: the OS can take a resource away from a process holding it

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: On a Linux system, new regular files are created with base permissions 666. If the user's umask is 027, what permissions does a newly created file get?

solution.explanation: The umask lists permission bits to remove. 666 with 027 removed: owner 6 - 0 = 6 (rw-), group 6 - 2 = 4 (r--), others 6 - 7 -> 0 (---). Result 640 = rw-r-----.
solution.shortcut: Files: 666 minus umask bits; directories: 777 minus umask bits.
solution.why_others_wrong: 750 (rwxr-x---) is what a new directory gets (777 with 027 removed); regular files never get execute from the base 666. 664 is the result of umask 002. 751 matches no step of the calculation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: At a supermarket billing counter, which input device reads the pattern of black and white lines printed on each product?

solution.explanation: A barcode reader shines light on the bars and reads the reflected pattern, which encodes the product number. The billing software then looks up the price.
solution.why_others_wrong: MICR reads magnetic-ink characters on cheques. A light pen points at a screen. A plotter is an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Monitors create colours by mixing red, green and blue light. Which colour model do colour printers use when mixing inks on paper?

solution.explanation: Screens emit light, so they use the additive RGB model. Printers put ink on white paper, which absorbs light, so they use the subtractive CMYK model. Black (K) is added because mixing C, M and Y does not give a deep black.
solution.why_others_wrong: RGB is the screen model. HSL is a way of describing colours in software, and YUV is used in video encoding, not in printer inks.
solution.final_answer: Option B: CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, black)

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which pointing device stays still on the desk while the user moves the pointer by rolling an exposed ball with the thumb or fingers?

solution.explanation: A trackball is like an upside-down mouse: the body stays in place and the user rolls the ball on top. It needs little desk space.
steps: Device fixed + ball rolled by hand = trackball
solution.why_others_wrong: A joystick uses a tilting lever, a touchpad senses a finger sliding on a flat surface, and a digitiser uses a pen on a tablet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A one-minute stereo (2-channel) audio clip is recorded without compression at a sampling rate of 44.1 kHz with 16 bits per sample. How much storage does it need?

solution.explanation: Size = sampling rate x bits per sample x channels x seconds / 8. 44,100 x 16 x 2 x 60 = 84,672,000 bits, and dividing by 8 gives 10,584,000 bytes (about 10.6 MB).
solution.why_others_wrong: 5,292,000 bytes counts only one channel. 1,323,000 bytes divides by 8 twice. 84,672,000 is the size in bits, not bytes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A digital photo of 3,000 x 2,000 pixels is printed at 300 DPI (dots per inch) with one pixel per dot. What is the size of the print?

solution.explanation: Each inch of paper holds 300 pixels. Width = 3,000 / 300 = 10 inches and height = 2,000 / 300 = 6.67 inches.
solution.why_others_wrong: 30 x 20 divides by 100 instead of 300. 1 x 0.67 divides by 3,000. 100 x 66.7 divides by 30.
solution.final_answer: Option D: 10 inches x about 6.67 inches

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which display technology needs no backlight because each pixel produces its own light, so that black pixels are completely switched off?

solution.explanation: In an OLED (Organic Light-Emitting Diode) display, every pixel emits light itself. A black pixel is simply off, which gives very deep blacks and allows thin, flexible screens.
solution.why_others_wrong: An LCD only blocks or passes light from a backlight, so it always needs one. A CRT fires an electron beam at phosphors from a tube, and a DLP projector reflects a lamp or laser light off tiny mirrors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: SRAM is faster and more expensive than DRAM and does not need refreshing. For which purpose is SRAM mainly used in a computer?

solution.explanation: SRAM stores each bit in a flip-flop, so it is fast and needs no refresh, but it takes more space and costs more. It is therefore used for small, fast caches inside the CPU, while cheaper DRAM is used for main memory.
solution.why_others_wrong: Main memory uses DRAM. Long-term storage uses HDDs or SSDs, and optical discs are read by a laser.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A pen drive (USB flash drive) stores data using which technology?

solution.explanation: A pen drive uses flash memory, a non-volatile semiconductor memory that keeps data without power and has no moving parts.
solution.why_others_wrong: Magnetic platters are used in hard disks, laser pits in CDs and DVDs, and magnetic tape in tape backups.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A hard disk is sold as 1 TB, where the manufacturer uses 1 TB = 10^12 bytes. The operating system counts in binary units (1 GB = 2^30 bytes). About how many GB does the operating system show?

solution.explanation: 10^12 / 2^30 = 1,000,000,000,000 / 1,073,741,824 = about 931. The disk is not missing space; the two sides simply use different definitions of a gigabyte.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1000 GB uses decimal units on both sides. 1024 GB wrongly assumes 1 TB = 1024 GB in this case. 977 mixes units (dividing by 1024 x 10^6).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which type of ROM is erased by exposing the chip to ultraviolet light through a small quartz window and can then be reprogrammed?

solution.explanation: EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM) is erased with strong UV light through a window on top of the chip, then reprogrammed with a special device.
solution.why_others_wrong: EEPROM is erased electrically. PROM can be programmed only once. Mask ROM is written at the factory and cannot be changed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: With a write-through cache policy, what happens when the CPU writes data to a block that is in the cache?

options.text: The data is written only to the cache and copied to main memory when the block is replaced
The data is written only to main memory and the cache block is deleted
The write waits until the cache is completely full
The data is written to both the cache and main memory at the same time

solution.explanation: Write-through updates the cache and main memory together, so memory is always up to date, at the cost of more memory traffic. Write-back updates only the cache and marks the block 'dirty'; memory is updated when the block is evicted.
steps: Write-back = cache now, memory on eviction
solution.why_others_wrong: Writing only to the cache until replacement is write-back. Write-through never skips the cache copy or deletes the block; it updates both. Caches never wait to fill up before writing.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The data is written to both the cache and main memory at the same time

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: On a hard disk platter, data is recorded on concentric circles, and each circle is divided into small arc-shaped units. What are the circles and units called?

solution.explanation: Each platter surface has concentric tracks, and each track is divided into sectors, the smallest unit the disk reads or writes. The same track on all surfaces forms a cylinder.
solution.why_others_wrong: A cluster is a group of sectors used by the file system. Pages and frames belong to virtual memory, not disk geometry.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A server stores identical copies of all data on two disks, so that it keeps working if one disk fails. Which RAID level is this?

solution.explanation: RAID 1 mirrors every write to two (or more) disks. Either disk alone holds the full data, so one disk failure loses nothing, though only half the raw capacity is usable.
steps: Identical copies on two disks = mirroring = RAID 1
solution.why_others_wrong: RAID 0 splits data across disks with no redundancy. RAID 5 needs at least three disks and stores parity, not full copies. RAID 6 stores two sets of parity across at least four disks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A hard disk has 4 platters and both surfaces of each platter store data. Each surface has 2,000 tracks, each track has 400 sectors, and each sector holds 512 bytes. What is the disk's capacity?

solution.concept: Disk capacity = surfaces x tracks x sectors x bytes per sector
solution.explanation: 4 platters x 2 surfaces = 8 surfaces. Capacity = 8 x 2,000 x 400 x 512 = 3,276,800,000 bytes (about 3.28 GB).
solution.why_others_wrong: 409,600,000 bytes counts one surface only. 1,638,400,000 bytes counts one surface per platter. 6,553,600,000 bytes counts 16 surfaces.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Websites such as Google Search and Bing, which find web pages matching the keywords you type, are called:

solution.explanation: A search engine indexes web pages and returns the ones that match a query. A browser is the program you use to open the search engine and other websites.
steps: Find pages for keywords = search engine
solution.why_others_wrong: A browser displays pages, a web server hosts them, and an operating system runs the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A file, such as a PDF statement, that is sent along with an email message is called a(n):

solution.explanation: An attachment is a file sent together with the email, usually shown with a paper-clip icon.
steps: File sent with an email = attachment
solution.why_others_wrong: A signature is the text block at the end of a message, the subject line summarises the message and the inbox is the folder that receives emails.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The main or starting page of a website, which usually opens first and links to its other pages, is called the:

solution.explanation: The home page is the main entry page of a website, for example the page that opens when you type only the domain name.
steps: Main starting page of a website = home page
solution.why_others_wrong: A portal is a website that gathers many services, a bookmark is a saved link in the browser, and the search bar is where queries are typed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Mail servers use DNS to find which server accepts email for a domain such as example.in. Which DNS record type provides this information?

solution.explanation: An MX (Mail Exchange) record names the host that accepts email for the domain, along with a preference number used when there are several mail servers.
steps: Mail server for a domain = MX record
solution.why_others_wrong: An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address, a CNAME gives an alias for another name, and a PTR record maps an address back to a name (reverse lookup).

fact_checks.claim: RFC 1035 defines the MX type (value 15) as 'mail exchange' and PTR (value 12) as a domain name pointer; MX data holds a preference and a host willing to act as mail exchange.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank adds DKIM to its outgoing email. What does DKIM let a receiving mail server check?

options.text: That the message has been encrypted so that only the recipient can read it
That the recipient's mailbox has enough free space for the message
That the message carries a valid cryptographic signature from the sending domain, using a public key published in that domain's DNS
That the sender typed a correct password into the bank's webmail

solution.explanation: DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) lets a domain take responsibility for a message by signing it. The receiver fetches the public key from the signer's DNS and verifies the signature, which shows the signed parts were not changed and that the domain vouched for the message. It helps detect spoofed mail.
steps: Sender's server signs the message with a private key
solution.why_others_wrong: DKIM signs messages; it does not encrypt them. It has nothing to do with mailbox space or with the sender's login password.
solution.final_answer: Option C: That the message carries a valid cryptographic signature from the sending domain, using a public key published in that domain's DNS

fact_checks.claim: RFC 6376: DKIM lets an organisation claim responsibility for a message by associating its domain with it, validated through a cryptographic signature and a public key retrieved from the signer's domain.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A net-banking site sets its session cookie with the HttpOnly attribute. What does this attribute do?

options.text: It makes the browser send the cookie only over unencrypted HTTP connections
It stops JavaScript running in the page from reading the cookie, reducing the damage from cross-site scripting
It deletes the cookie as soon as the page finishes loading
It encrypts the cookie's value with the user's password

solution.explanation: HttpOnly forbids scripts from accessing the cookie (for example through document.cookie), though the browser still sends it with requests. An attacker who injects JavaScript into the page then cannot simply read and steal the session cookie.
steps: Protects session cookies against XSS theft
solution.why_others_wrong: Sending a cookie only over HTTPS is the job of the Secure attribute, not HttpOnly, and HttpOnly certainly does not force plain HTTP. It does not delete or encrypt the cookie.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It stops JavaScript running in the page from reading the cookie, reducing the damage from cross-site scripting

fact_checks.claim: MDN Set-Cookie: HttpOnly forbids JavaScript from accessing the cookie, for example through Document.cookie, which mitigates attacks against cross-site scripting.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: HTTP is described as a 'stateless' protocol. What does this mean?

options.text: HTTP cannot carry any data from the client to the server
The server never stores any files
Each request is handled independently, with no built-in link to earlier requests; sessions need extra mechanisms such as cookies
The connection is always encrypted, so no state can be seen

solution.explanation: In plain HTTP there is no link between two successive requests, even on the same connection. Websites add state, such as a login session or a shopping basket, by using cookies in the headers.
steps: Stateless = no memory of earlier requests in the protocol itself
solution.why_others_wrong: HTTP does carry data from client to server (for example in a POST body). 'Stateless' says nothing about storing files or about encryption; encryption comes from HTTPS/TLS.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Each request is handled independently, with no built-in link to earlier requests; sessions need extra mechanisms such as cookies

fact_checks.claim: MDN: HTTP is stateless, with no link between two requests successively carried out on the same connection; HTTP cookies allow the use of stateful sessions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which network device receives a weakened signal and regenerates it at full strength, so that a cable can run beyond its normal maximum distance?

solution.explanation: A repeater works at the physical layer. It regenerates the signal it receives so the network can cover a longer distance; it does not read addresses.
steps: Regenerate weak signal to extend distance = repeater
solution.why_others_wrong: A router forwards packets between networks using IP addresses, a firewall filters traffic and a modem converts digital signals for a telephone or cable line.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which OSI layer sets up, manages and ends the dialogue (session) between two applications, and can add checkpoints so that a long transfer resumes from the last checkpoint after a failure?

solution.explanation: The session layer (layer 5) handles dialogue control and synchronisation: it opens, manages and closes sessions and inserts checkpoints for recovery.
solution.why_others_wrong: The transport layer gives end-to-end delivery and error control. The application layer provides services to users. The network layer handles logical addressing and routing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A computer knows the IPv4 address of another machine on its LAN but needs that machine's MAC address to send it an Ethernet frame. Which protocol finds the MAC address?

solution.explanation: ARP broadcasts 'who has this IP address?' on the local network, and the owner replies with its MAC address, which is then cached.
steps: IP address known, MAC needed = ARP
solution.why_others_wrong: DNS maps names to IP addresses, DHCP hands out IP addresses, and ICMP carries error and diagnostic messages such as ping.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch LAN must support 500 hosts in one IPv4 subnet. What is the longest prefix (smallest subnet) that provides at least 500 usable host addresses?

solution.explanation: Usable hosts = 2^(32 - prefix) - 2. A /24 gives 254 (too few). A /23 gives 2^9 - 2 = 510, enough. A /22 gives 1,022, which also works but is larger than needed.
solution.shortcut: Find the smallest power of 2 above 501: 512 = 2^9, so the prefix is 32 - 9.
solution.why_others_wrong: /22 gives 1,022 hosts, not the smallest subnet. /24 gives 254 and /25 gives 126, both too few.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Following RFC 5952's rules for writing IPv6 addresses as text, what is the canonical form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329?

solution.explanation: RFC 5952 requires leading zeros in each 16-bit group to be removed (0db8 -> db8, 0042 -> 42) and the longest run of all-zero groups to be replaced by '::'. The three zero groups become '::', giving 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329.
steps: Replace the run of zero groups with ::
solution.why_others_wrong: 2001:db8::ff00:0042:8329 keeps a leading zero, which RFC 5952 forbids. 2001:db8::ff:42:8329 removes trailing zeros from ff00, which changes the address. 2001:db8:0:0:0:ff00:42:8329 is valid but does not use '::' as required.

fact_checks.claim: RFC 5952: leading zeros MUST be suppressed; '::' MUST be used to its maximum capability on the longest run of zero fields; hex digits MUST be lowercase.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Software that keeps showing unwanted pop-up advertisements on a user's computer, often installed bundled with free programs, is called:

solution.explanation: Adware displays unwanted advertisements, often bundled with free software, and may also track browsing to target the ads.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ransomware locks files for payment, firmware is legitimate device software and a worm spreads itself across networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A large number of infected computers secretly controlled by an attacker, for example to send spam or flood a website with traffic, is called a:

solution.explanation: A botnet is a network of compromised computers ('bots' or 'zombies') remotely controlled by an attacker, often used for spam and distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.
steps: Many infected machines under remote control = botnet
solution.why_others_wrong: A firewall filters network traffic, an intranet is an organisation's private network and a sandbox is an isolated area for safely running untrusted programs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An attacker leaves a USB pen drive labelled 'Salary details 2026' in a bank's car park, hoping an employee will plug it into an office computer. This social-engineering trick is called:

solution.explanation: Baiting lures victims with something tempting, such as an infected pen drive or a free download, so that they install malware themselves.
steps: Tempting item left to be picked up = baiting
solution.why_others_wrong: Vishing uses phone calls, pharming redirects website traffic through DNS tampering, and shoulder surfing is watching someone type.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which of these is the strongest password?

solution.explanation: A strong password is long and mixes upper-case and lower-case letters, digits and symbols, without dictionary words, names or dates. T7#qL!9vR2@m meets all these conditions.
steps: Long + mixed character types + no words or dates = strong
solution.why_others_wrong: password123 and 12345678 are among the most commonly guessed passwords, and Rahul1990 is a name plus a year, which is easy to guess.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A phishing email aimed specifically at a bank's Chairman and Managing Director, pretending to be a legal notice, is a type of spear phishing known as:

solution.explanation: Whaling targets senior executives ('big fish'), whose access and authority make them valuable targets. The messages are carefully tailored, such as fake legal or regulatory notices.
steps: Phishing aimed at top executives = whaling
solution.why_others_wrong: Smishing uses SMS, baiting uses tempting items such as infected pen drives and tailgating is following someone through a secured door.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which type of malware hides deep inside the operating system, often with administrator-level access, and conceals its own files and processes so that ordinary tools cannot detect it?

solution.explanation: A rootkit gives an attacker privileged ('root') control and modifies the operating system to hide itself and other malware. Removing it often needs special tools or reinstalling the OS.
steps: Hidden in OS + privileged access + conceals itself = rootkit
solution.why_others_wrong: Adware shows ads, a worm spreads over networks, and spam is unwanted bulk email, not malware that hides in the OS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A dismissed programmer hides code in a payroll system that will delete records on 1 April if his employee ID is no longer present. Malicious code that waits for a specific date or condition before acting is called a:

solution.explanation: A logic bomb lies dormant inside a legitimate program until a trigger condition, such as a date or an event, occurs, and then carries out its harmful action.
solution.why_others_wrong: A botnet is a network of infected machines, a keylogger records keystrokes, and a cookie is a small browser data file.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An unauthorised person follows a bank employee closely through a door that opens only with an access card, without using a card of his own. This physical social-engineering technique is called:

solution.explanation: Tailgating means entering a restricted area by following an authorised person through a secured entrance. Staff are trained not to hold access-controlled doors for others.
steps: Following someone through a secured door = tailgating
solution.why_others_wrong: Pretexting is inventing a false story to get information, phishing uses fake messages and spoofing fakes an identity such as an email address or caller ID.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An authenticator app on a phone shows a 6-digit code that changes every 30 seconds and works even without a network connection. The code is calculated from a secret shared with the server and the current time. This is called a:

solution.explanation: TOTP (RFC 6238) computes a short-lived one-time password from a shared secret key and the current time, divided into time steps (30 seconds by default). Phone and server calculate the same code independently, so no network is needed on the phone.
steps: Changes every time step (default 30 s) = TOTP
solution.why_others_wrong: A static PIN never changes. A CAPTCHA tells humans from bots. A digital certificate binds a public key to an identity; it does not produce changing codes.

fact_checks.claim: RFC 6238 defines TOTP, a time-based variant of the OTP algorithm giving short-lived OTP values; the time step X has a default value of 30 seconds; K is the shared secret.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Attackers exploit a security flaw in a widely used application before its vendor knows about it or has released a patch. Such a flaw is called a:

solution.explanation: A zero-day is a vulnerability unknown to the vendor, so defenders have had 'zero days' to fix it. Attacks using it can succeed even against fully updated systems.
steps: Flaw exploited before vendor knows / patch exists = zero-day
solution.why_others_wrong: A logic bomb is planted malicious code with a trigger. A firewall rule and a digital signature are security controls, not flaws.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Before storing passwords as hashes, a bank's system adds a random value, unique to each user, to each password. What is the main benefit of this 'salt'?

options.text: It lets the bank decrypt the stored password whenever needed
Users with the same password get different hashes, which defeats precomputed (rainbow table) attacks
It makes the hash shorter so it needs less storage
It removes the need for users to choose strong passwords

solution.explanation: A unique salt changes the input to the hash function for each user. Two identical passwords then produce different hashes, and an attacker cannot use one precomputed table of hashes for every account but must attack each one separately.
steps: hash(salt + password) stored with the salt
Same password, different salt -> different hash
solution.why_others_wrong: Hashes are one-way, so salting does not allow decryption. The hash length is fixed by the algorithm. Weak passwords can still be guessed one account at a time.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Users with the same password get different hashes, which defeats precomputed (rainbow table) attacks

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a Caesar cipher, each letter is replaced by the letter a fixed number of places later in the alphabet, wrapping from Z back to A. With a shift of 3, how is the word LOAN encrypted?

solution.explanation: Shift each letter 3 places forward: L -> O, O -> R, A -> D, N -> Q. The ciphertext is ORDQ.
solution.why_others_wrong: ILXK shifts 3 places backwards (decryption direction). MPBO shifts by only 1. ORDP shifts the last letter by 2 instead of 3.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What problem does the Diffie-Hellman key exchange solve?

options.text: It proves that a document has not changed by producing a fixed-length hash
It stores passwords safely in a database
It lets two parties agree on a shared secret key over an insecure channel without ever sending the key itself

solution.explanation: In Diffie-Hellman, each side combines its own private value with public values exchanged openly. Both arrive at the same secret, while an eavesdropper who sees only the public values cannot feasibly compute it. The shared secret is then used for fast symmetric encryption, as in TLS.
steps: Each side combines them with its private value
Both get the same shared secret key
solution.why_others_wrong: Compression is unrelated to key exchange. Producing a fixed-length digest is what a hash function does. Password storage uses salted hashing.
solution.final_answer: Option D: It lets two parties agree on a shared secret key over an insecure channel without ever sending the key itself

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A virus changes its own code (for example by re-encrypting itself with a new key) every time it infects a new file, so that no two copies look alike and signature-based antivirus finds it hard to detect. This is a:

solution.explanation: A polymorphic virus mutates its appearance with each infection while keeping the same behaviour. Because a fixed byte pattern cannot match every copy, defenders rely on behaviour-based and heuristic detection.
steps: Code changes with each infection to dodge signatures = polymorphic
solution.why_others_wrong: A boot sector virus is defined by where it lives (the boot sector). A macro virus spreads through document macros. A logic bomb waits for a trigger; none of these is defined by changing its code.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which SQL command adds a new row of data to a table?

solution.explanation: INSERT INTO table VALUES (...) adds new rows. UPDATE changes values in existing rows.
solution.why_others_wrong: UPDATE modifies existing rows, ALTER changes a table's structure and CREATE makes a new table or other object.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a table Attendance(EmployeeID, Date, Status), neither EmployeeID nor Date alone is unique, but the pair (EmployeeID, Date) is. A primary key made of two or more columns like this is called a:

solution.explanation: A composite key uses two or more columns together to identify each row uniquely, because no single column can do it alone.
steps: Two columns together unique = composite key
solution.why_others_wrong: A foreign key refers to another table's key. An alternate key is a candidate key not chosen as primary. A surrogate key is an artificial single column such as an auto-number ID.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The SQL commands GRANT and REVOKE, which give and take away users' permissions on database objects, belong to which category?

solution.explanation: DCL commands control access rights: GRANT gives privileges and REVOKE removes them.
solution.why_others_wrong: DDL defines structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP), DML works on data (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) and TCL manages transactions (COMMIT, ROLLBACK).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Table Txn has six rows with these values of amount: 999, 1000, 2500, NULL, 5000, 7000. What does this query return? SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Txn WHERE amount NOT BETWEEN 1000 AND 5000;

solution.concept: BETWEEN is inclusive; comparisons with NULL are unknown
solution.explanation: BETWEEN 1000 AND 5000 includes both end values, so 1000, 2500 and 5000 are inside the range. NOT BETWEEN keeps 999 and 7000. For the NULL row the condition is UNKNOWN, not TRUE, so WHERE drops it. The count is 2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 wrongly counts the NULL row. 4 treats BETWEEN as exclusive (adding 1000 and 5000). 5 makes both mistakes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In MS Word, which keyboard shortcut inserts a hyperlink?

solution.explanation: Ctrl + K opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog in Word.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ctrl + H opens Replace, Ctrl + L left-aligns text and Ctrl + Y redoes or repeats the last action.

fact_checks.claim: Word for Windows: Ctrl+K inserts a hyperlink.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which character is normally typed first to begin a formula in an Excel cell?

solution.explanation: Excel treats an entry starting with = as a formula, for example =A1+B1. Without it, the entry is stored as text or a number.
solution.why_others_wrong: # begins error values such as #REF!, & joins text inside a formula, and $ makes a cell reference absolute.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In PowerPoint, which shortcut starts the slide show from the CURRENT slide rather than from the first slide?

solution.explanation: Shift + F5 starts the presentation from the slide currently selected. F5 alone starts from the beginning.
solution.why_others_wrong: F5 starts from the first slide. Ctrl + F5 is not the slide-show shortcut, and Alt + F4 closes the window.

fact_checks.claim: PowerPoint: Shift+F5 starts a presentation from the current slide.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In MS Word, which keyboard shortcut opens the dialog to find a word and replace it with another throughout the document?

solution.explanation: Ctrl + H opens the Replace dialog box, used to find and replace text, formatting or special items.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ctrl + F opens the Navigation pane for finding only, Ctrl + R right-aligns a paragraph and Ctrl + G opens Go To.

fact_checks.claim: Word for Windows: Ctrl+H displays the Replace dialog box to find and replace text, specific formatting or special items.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An Excel sheet has 2,000 rows of customer data. Which feature keeps the heading row visible at the top while the user scrolls down?

solution.explanation: View > Freeze Panes (or Freeze Top Row) locks rows and/or columns so they stay on screen while the rest of the sheet scrolls.
steps: Keep heading visible while scrolling = Freeze Panes
solution.why_others_wrong: Wrap Text shows long text on several lines in a cell, Merge & Center joins cells, and Sort & Filter reorders or hides rows; none keeps the heading on screen.

fact_checks.claim: Excel's Freeze Panes locks rows, columns or both to the top and left of the sheet so they stay visible while scrolling (View > Freeze Panes).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Cells A1 to A6 contain 45, 82, 67, 82, 30 and 91. What does =LARGE(A1:A6, 3) return?

solution.explanation: LARGE(range, k) returns the k-th largest value, counting duplicates separately. Sorted from the top: 91, 82, 82, 67, 45, 30. The third value is 82.
solution.why_others_wrong: 67 would be the answer only if duplicates were counted once. 91 is the largest and 45 the 5th largest.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: B2:B6 contain the names Asha, Ravi, Meena, John and Farah, and C2:C6 contain their balances 52000, 87000, 61000, 87500 and 43000. What does =INDEX(B2:B6, MATCH(MAX(C2:C6), C2:C6, 0)) return?

solution.explanation: MAX(C2:C6) = 87500. MATCH(87500, C2:C6, 0) finds its exact position, 4. INDEX(B2:B6, 4) returns the 4th name, John.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ravi has 87000, just below the maximum. Meena is the middle row and Farah the last row; neither has the highest balance.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A2:A9 holds branches and B2:B9 amounts: Pune 45000, Delhi 72000, Pune 50000, Agra 90000, Pune 81000, Delhi 30000, Pune 49999, Delhi 50000. What does =COUNTIFS(A2:A9, "Pune", B2:B9, ">=50000") return?

solution.explanation: COUNTIFS counts rows that meet every condition. Pune rows: 45000, 50000, 81000, 49999. Of these, only 50000 and 81000 are >= 50000, so the result is 2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 treats >= as > (dropping 50000). 4 counts all Pune rows. 5 counts all amounts >= 50000 in any branch.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: B2:B4 contain quantities 12, 5 and 8, and C2:C4 contain unit rates 150, 420 and 75. What does =SUMPRODUCT(B2:B4, C2:C4) return?

solution.explanation: SUMPRODUCT multiplies matching items and adds the products: 12 x 150 + 5 x 420 + 8 x 75 = 1800 + 2100 + 600 = 4500.
solution.why_others_wrong: 670 adds all the numbers. 2100 is only the largest single product. 16125 multiplies the two totals (25 x 645).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Cell D2 contains =SUM(A2,B2,C2). The user then deletes column B. Which error value does the formula now show?

solution.explanation: When a cell that a formula refers to explicitly is deleted, the reference is no longer valid and Excel shows #REF!. Using a range such as =SUM(A2:C2) instead would simply shrink and avoid the error.
steps: Explicit reference to a deleted cell
solution.why_others_wrong: #VALUE! comes from the wrong type of argument, #NAME? from an unrecognised function or name, and #DIV/0! from dividing by zero.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: #REF! appears when a formula refers to a cell that is not valid, most often when referenced cells are deleted; =SUM(B2,C2,D2) returns #REF! if a referenced column is deleted.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: At a small shop, a customer pays through UPI by pointing her phone camera at a square printed pattern displayed at the counter. What is this pattern called?

solution.explanation: A QR (Quick Response) code is a two-dimensional code that stores the merchant's payment details. The UPI app reads it so the customer need not type the payee's address.
steps: Square pattern scanned for UPI = QR code
solution.why_others_wrong: A barcode is one-dimensional lines on products. Holograms and watermarks are anti-counterfeiting marks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: How does a dynamic QR code at a merchant's billing counter differ from a static QR code pasted on the wall?

options.text: It can be scanned only by debit cards
It works without any bank account behind it
It never changes, so it can be printed once and used forever
It is generated for each transaction and already contains that bill's amount and reference

solution.explanation: A static QR code holds only the merchant's details; the customer types the amount. A dynamic QR code is generated for each sale and carries the amount and a transaction reference, which reduces errors and makes reconciliation easier.
steps: Static = merchant details only, customer enters amount
Dynamic = new code per bill with amount
solution.why_others_wrong: QR codes are scanned by phone apps, not cards. Every QR payment settles to a bank account. A code that never changes is a static QR.
solution.final_answer: Option D: It is generated for each transaction and already contains that bill's amount and reference

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which security standard must merchants, payment processors and banks follow when they store, process or transmit payment-card data?

solution.explanation: PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard), maintained by the PCI Security Standards Council, sets requirements for protecting cardholder data, such as encryption, access control and monitoring.
steps: Card data protection standard = PCI DSS
solution.why_others_wrong: ISO 9001 is a quality-management standard, HTML5 is a web markup language and IEEE 802.11 is the Wi-Fi standard.

fact_checks.claim: The PCI Security Standards Council's PCI DSS governs storage of card data; it prohibits storing card verification codes after authorization.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An online shop wants to keep each customer's card verification code (CVV/CVC) on file after the first payment so that repeat purchases are faster, and customers have agreed. Under PCI DSS, is this allowed?

options.text: Yes, if the code is encrypted
No; card verification codes must not be stored after authorization, even if encrypted or if the customer agrees
Yes, if the customer has given written permission
Yes, but only for recurring payments such as subscriptions

solution.concept: Sensitive authentication data under PCI DSS
solution.explanation: The card verification code is sensitive authentication data. PCI DSS forbids storing it after authorization, even in encrypted form, and customer permission does not change this. It is not needed for card-on-file or recurring payments, which instead use stored card data or tokens.
steps: Encryption or customer consent does not make it allowed
solution.why_others_wrong: Encryption does not lift the ban; customer permission does not lift it; and recurring payments do not need the code, so storing it for them is also prohibited.
solution.final_answer: Option B: No; card verification codes must not be stored after authorization, even if encrypted or if the customer agrees

fact_checks.claim: PCI SSC FAQ: card verification codes are not needed for card-on-file or recurring transactions and storing them for these purposes is prohibited, regardless of any permission from the customer; the ban on storing sensitive authentication data after authorization applies even if it is encrypted.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What does GUI stand for?

solution.explanation: A GUI (Graphical User Interface) lets users work with windows, icons, menus and a pointer instead of typed commands.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What is the full form of USB?

solution.explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus) is the standard port and cable system for connecting peripherals and charging devices.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A network connecting the computers inside one bank branch is a LAN. What does LAN stand for?

solution.explanation: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small area such as an office, branch or building. A WAN (Wide Area Network) links distant sites.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What is the full form of WWW?

solution.explanation: WWW (World Wide Web) is the system of linked web pages accessed over the internet with a browser.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are incorrect word orders or made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What does HTTP stand for?

solution.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the protocol browsers and web servers use to exchange web pages; HTTPS is its secure version over TLS.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The company that provides a home or office with its internet connection is called an ISP. What does ISP stand for?

solution.explanation: An ISP (Internet Service Provider) gives customers access to the internet through broadband, fibre or mobile data.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Photographs are commonly saved in the JPEG format. What does JPEG stand for?

solution.explanation: JPEG is named after the Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee that created this lossy image-compression standard.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Joint Photographic Experts Group

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Internet banking sends a one-time code to the registered mobile number to confirm a transaction. What does OTP stand for?

solution.explanation: An OTP (One-Time Password) is valid for only one login or transaction, usually for a short time.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Modern PCs use UEFI firmware instead of the older BIOS. What does UEFI stand for?

solution.explanation: UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) is a specification, maintained by the UEFI Forum, for the interface between the operating system and platform firmware. It replaces the legacy BIOS and supports features such as Secure Boot.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface

fact_checks.claim: The UEFI Forum publishes the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) specification at uefi.org.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Branches increasingly make phone calls over their data network instead of traditional telephone lines, using VoIP. What does VoIP stand for?

solution.explanation: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) carries voice calls as data packets over IP networks such as the internet or a bank's WAN.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Voice over Internet Protocol
